reviews.text: In the Coastal Cave, during the fight with Zohak The Vile, I noticed the main character's skeleton was clearly able to move itself without any muscles. I mean, what are we to believe, that this is some sort of magic barbarian or something? Boy, I sure hope someone was fired for that blunder.

[i] The nude mode sold me on the game. Being able to swing your massive balls and crush enemies is peak gameplay [spoiler]one of your abilities has spiked balls spinning around you, get your mind out of the gutter[/spoiler]! In all seriousness, Conquest Dark is a survivors like that leans heavily into ARPG genre, offering a crazy number of builds and a deep itemisation system, and plenty of ways to min-max as you cause a skeleton genocide. [/i] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions, followed by the Review:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + I’m a sucker for the endless rituals + Toggleable auto aim and on click priority targeting + Multiple meta progression systems with different ways to progress through them + Melee and ranged builds are both viable (my favourite is playing as a leaping barbarian) + I love how small the experience and health globes are, there’s next to no impact on visibility + Ritual modifiers keep things fresh, letting you increase difficulty and rewards as you please (corruption) + 27 Runes which can be collected, imbued to your skills, and upgraded, further empowering your abilities + The map is designed brilliantly, slowly unlocking additional rituals, characters, and systems as you progress + Multiple classes – Barbarian, Thief, Hunter, Oathkeeper, and Acolyte of Kuu – Across three races, each with their own unique masteries (28 total) + Racial traits, class bonuses, proficiencies, and masteries, along with item levels, rarities, sets, and different damage types add a heap of customisation 🟥 Cons: - The single event becomes repetitive - Enemy projectiles can get lost in the fray - Enemies suddenly become damage sponges - The tight arena maps may be too small for some - Some may not like the bleeding mechanic where you lose a % of health each second, stacking with each death - Damage taken feels too high, which could cause newcomers to feel melee isn’t viable (going as far as calling it bad and broken) - Rituals start slow until you unlock your first power ability, and the game doesn’t truly open up until the first few hours have passed and you’ve unlocked more systems 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Larger maps ~ Add achievements ~ Add more abilities ~ Let us collect armour & weapons ~ Toggle to highlight enemy projectiles ~ Toggle to disable slowly turning into a skeleton as you lose lives ~ Crafting/forging systems could lean more into the ARPG systems ~ As rerolling is infinite when selecting your character, origin, and weapon, why not let us assign these at the start? [h1] As Soon as I Saw Nude Mode, I Was Sold [/h1] Conquest Dark (CD) is similar to survivors likes before it, so why should you try it? If you’re a fan of ARPGs, CD is a must – It leans heavily into genre, offering a crazy number of builds and a deep itemisation system. Additionally, the bleeding mechanic means you can’t simply AFK while the game plays itself. The bleeding mechanic is the most controversial aspect of CD. Basically, you have 10 lives and upon dying, you gain 1 bleeding stack, with each stack reducing your maximum HP by 1% each second. Unfortunately, stacks cannot be removed, however, bleed reduction upgrades, health drops, and regeneration skills can help you survive. Early on bleed is a PITA, but with experience you’ll learn to manage and survive the tedium of constantly losing health. This mechanic is frustrating and punishing, but at the same time, most other survivors likes have me becoming OP and simply AFKing until the level completes itself. [h1] Builds Reminiscent of ARPGs Like Diablo, Last Epoch, and POE [/h1] CD is basically an ARPG survivors like – Select a character, origin story, and weapon, with abilities and passives (mastery upgrades) being given upon level up. With 20 primary, 18 power, 15 passive, and 12 movement abilities, along with items and runes, there’s a heap of build variety. To give you an idea, here are some of the builds I played below: [list] [*] Barbarian – I had two builds, both reminiscent of Diablo. One was a leap, dealing AOE damage upon landing, while the other was HotA, sending AOE shockwaves with every attack. [*] Hunter – Imagine a high crit, multi shot god, where every projectile had a chance to split in two. My screen was filled with piercing projectiles and dead skeletons. [*] Oathkeeper – One word, Hammerdin. AOE hammers constantly span around my character, killing anything they came in contact with. [/list] I recommend CD for fans of survivors likes who love ARPGs. It starts off slow, but progression occurs at a steady pace, always having you say, “just one more run”. While it’s not the best survivors like I’ve played, I rank it well above many others – Give it a try, the two-hour refund window is more than enough time to decide if CD is for you. Generally I feel like the game is close to being great but not quite there. Some questionable design decisions hold it back. 1. Lack of choice. This does open up as the game progresses and you unlock more things but early game you are really railroaded into a single build. Choosing between hardly meaningful passive stat changes. Even later in the game as you unlock more classes you generally end up locked into very similar hardly different choices. 2. Meta progression System encourages you to run the same build again and again. Your meta progression falls into three categories. One is just generally getting stronger via red stones. Two is getting stronger via "factions" which really means playing the same class again and again. The classes have limited weapon choice so it ends up being play the same weapons again and again until you max out the faction. Third is upgrading weapons, which again encourages you into playing the same weapons. This means you generally are rewarded from doing the same thing over and over and it gets bland fast. Great games in this genre do things that encourage you to try different things every single run. 3. The enemies really aren't threatening in interesting ways. Everything moves slow, everything attacks slow. It's fairly easy to stack one or two defensive passives and just wait fro the inevitable win. 4. Abilities / passives don't really interact in interesting ways. They're just stats. They're aren't combos to learn or item paths to try. The one thing I felt was unique about this game and was fun was leaping as a barbarian and having to melee enemies to build up energy to hit big power attacks. It was something uniquely fun I hadn't experience in other games in the genre. Overall it didn't really hook me and I can't recommend it against the other choices in the genre. The game has good bones though so I think revamping and revisiting some of the systems could make it a completely different game easily.

Played the demo back when it was available and loved the game and its potential Now in early access, and i still like the game and see a lot of potential, but this bleed mechanic they came up with makes no sense in any capacity and diminishes all the fun that this game is packing. A simplified explanation of bleed: Its a dot mechanic. You have 10 health bars. You can heal only within the current health bar. Every time you lose a health bar you get 1 bleed stack. The lower on health bars you go the more dot damage you take. On the last health bar you might as well not have health if unless you specifically build bleed resits ( if you roll some ) through the roof. Even then it is still annoying. If they were looking to add up some difficulty, i'd rather have them give us 5 health bars without the bleed mechanic instead of 10 with bleed. This mechanic and the focus on it doesn't add anything in terms of difficulty. It is just not fun and plain annoying. Will keep monitoring this game and see where they go and change this review in the future.

Mind-numbingly grindy and one-track. Progression will be "normal" until level 20 in any faction or racetrack node ( the ones where you have to walk in a really big circle until about ~20 seconds are left on the clock, then advance the ritual tier ) and/or when you get to the rituals that have +10% spawn frequency and +50% enemy health/damage, then the game's cracks REALLY show. See, the dev basically showed his hand with the most recent update that, very gently paraphrased, "made unoptimized/unoptimal builds no longer viable" , in a game where "viable" is one of about four builds, and only if you've grinded enough soul coins on the right weapons to have three rune slots on every item, ability, and passive that you're going to use. The mechanic in question was the "rage" mechanic on bosses, which was added in response to people saying things were too hard and those bosses were taking too long (especially since he earlier added a thing where bosses cannot be nuked but you still can- if you do enough damage to clear a healthbar, they get to get to the next healthbar without taking the rest of the damage, but you get nuked like normal). I'm not joking. Smooth out the difficulty curve a bit? Nope. Increase the number of non-meta builds that work? Nope. Add something that actually FURTHER LIMITS POSSIBLE BUILDS?. Dev decided to. Against this, the soul coin grind was reduced *A LITTLE*. It still takes over 20+ hours to make everything viable at the point you need it to be, that's still not OK, especially not for a grindy moment-to-moment choice Roguelike. On that topic, stat shrines that had a guaranteed flat increase with a scaling amount of bloodstone needed to increase them over time.... were changed into RNG shrines that have 3 rollable values on them that can't even have their individual stats locked. Why was this done? Because dev saw that people weren't spending bloodstone because the costs were getting too high. Could have just taken the normal route and had a high flat value instead of going nuclear about it but OK I GUESS. (Nobody likes this change, by the way. Comments under the update, disscussions posts, it's the Bleed Mechanic all over again.) You may be wondering about the Grindy accusation. Let me put it this way: when you reach that level of progression, it takes increasing the difficulty (you know, making the game EVEN HARDER so that you can grind AT THAT HARD LEVEL to then unscale the difficulty and get what you need to done) , and then doing long runs that need you to have already grinded in order to grind the progression out, but when you go to do that...... it takes hour-long runs to even get single levels in racetrack nodes and faction XP, and it's grueling and miniscule choice after miniscule choice after miniscule choice the whole way through. It's not fun, it's boring, time-consuming, and grindy for no good reason. I don't have very much faith in future updates, especially since the updates right out of the gate were all focused on the bleed mechanic and not the 50+ hour total grind to make things viable, and now the first "major" one took away a precious source of player power, added some hyper-rare rng equipment, made the already hard and sloggy bosses EVEN HARDER, and baaaarely moved the needle on the coin grind. 2/10 until that egregious grind/difficulty (inflated enemy/boss hp) gets addressed and dev stops making weird descisions.

Usually the first thing I do when I play a game for the first time is to go through all the settings to customize them how I want before I start playing. So I did that, and while I was going through I saw an option for "Allow Nudity," So I thought, "Well, this seems like a mostly serious semi-realistic Conan-type setting, so there's probably topless harpies or zombie butts or something. Considerate of the dev to think of streamers and youtube videos and such and give them an option to disable it, but I'm a mature adult in my own home so I'll turn that on." I finished my settings and got into the game, and read the very serious and clearly deeply thought-out world intro, and read some of the tutorial index, and then I started up my first game. And when I loaded in, right in the middle of the screen was my randomized character, and front and center in the character portrait was his ENORMOUS low-poly dongus just danglin' in the breeze. And I mean HUGE. It looked like a pink traffic cone. It was like he had a third leg that was amputated at the knee. He should have had to lean backwards at a 45 degree angle just to keep from falling on his face. That solid minute of uncontrollable laughter alone was worth the price of admission. Game has promise and plays well but has a fatal flaw. The end boss is structured completely differently from the rest of the game. To be specific: every other boss pauses the timer and you fight them, then the timer begins counting down again. The final boss instead gives you a timer that just kills you after it elapses. So if your build isn't capable of ultra fast killing a single target it won't work. Builds and playstyle that work on the rest of the game will never be able to complete that boss. I don't mean it'll be hard. I mean that there are vanishingly few viable builds to beat the final boss. If you care about being able to complete a game stay away (at least for now).

**Recommended** I received a review copy of Conquest Dark through Keymailer. As always, getting a free copy doesn't change my opinion. If I don't like a game, I'll say it. Thankfully... that wasn't the case here. Conquest Dark ended up being one of my favorite survivor-like games that I've played in a while. I knew I was probably going to enjoy it within the first couple of minutes. You literally start with nothing. No armor, no weapons... just your fists. Then you spot a skeleton carrying a weapon, beat him up, steal his gear, and that's basically the beginning of your adventure. I don't know why, but I thought that was a really cool way to start the game. Instead of just surviving endless waves forever, you're actually completing rituals. You fight through hordes of enemies, level up, find gear, upgrade abilities, defeat bosses, and eventually finish the ritual before moving on. I really liked having an actual goal instead of just surviving until I got bored. One of my favorite things is that your gear actually changes how your character looks. It sounds simple, but I always appreciate games that let me see my character getting stronger instead of just watching numbers go up. I've only scratched the surface so far, but it already feels like there's a lot here. Different gear sets, different abilities, plenty of ways to experiment with builds, multiple environments, mini-bosses, full bosses... every run feels like I'm finding something new. The atmosphere is also fantastic. The darker art style works really well, and the world has a gritty fantasy feel that immediately pulled me in. I also noticed there's an AI build system that lets you share and try different builds. I haven't really messed with it yet, but I think it's a really cool feature to include, especially once the community starts putting together some crazy combinations. Honestly... this is one of those games I find myself playing even when I'm not recording videos. To me, that's usually a pretty good sign. If you're a fan of survivor-likes, action RPGs, or games that let you constantly experiment with different builds, I think Conquest Dark is absolutely worth checking out. --- If you're interested in seeing my full thoughts, I also have a **RawImpressions** review on YouTube. I cover honest gaming reviews, first impressions, and trailer reactions over there if that's your kind of thing.
